symbols.name: kernel scalar a
symbols.meaning: The first scalar of the two-point kernel $aI+bX$, not the real numerator part of a Gaussian dyadic.
symbols.quote: Each kernel is $aI+bX$, where $a$ and $b$ are the two scalars of the kernel, not the numerator parts bound earlier.

symbols.name: kernel scalar b
symbols.meaning: The second scalar of the two-point kernel $aI+bX$, not the imaginary numerator part of a Gaussian dyadic.
symbols.quote: Each kernel is $aI+bX$, where $a$ and $b$ are the two scalars of the kernel, not the numerator parts bound earlier.

symbols.name: two-point identity
symbols.meaning: The identity map on two points, the identity part of the kernel.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels, built from $I$, the identity on two points, and $X$, the map that swaps the two points.

symbols.name: two-point swap
symbols.meaning: The map that swaps the two points, the swap part of the kernel.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels, built from $I$, the identity on two points, and $X$, the map that swaps the two points.

relations.quote: A complex phase network is built on a [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md) with a frame change on each edge, and it turns the completed complex layer into the simultaneous $H_0$ layer.
Each frame change takes its scalars from [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), so every sum and product stays exact, with no rounding.
Each wire is labelled by [Subspace labels](subspace-labels.md).
Applied to all selected address bits at once, the network is a [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) of one kernel per bit, evaluated on all addresses.
